Integration with electronic health records via standard medical data communication protocols (HL7, FHIR, etc.) would make it possible to automatically retrieve the necessary information (vital signs, tests) and return the probability calculation in the form of an alert in the patient’s electronic health record.

This approach is compatible with the Human in the Loop (HITL) paradigm, where humans remain in charge of the final decision and can choose to accept, reject, or modify the model’s recommendation without being relegated to the role of mere spectators [ 23 , 27 , 28 ].
Future studies will also need to evaluate how the use of a BN fits into the workflow without increasing the cognitive load or generating excessive alerts.

Where a conventional algorithm would force an opaque score (sepsis 80%) or a binary decision (sepsis vs. no sepsis), BNs produce an explicit conditional probability that is updated with each new piece of information, providing a confidence interval for the prediction (probability of sepsis between 80 and 95%).

unlisted_practices: Involve healthcare professionals from the design stage of AI models, in line with the Human-in-the-Loop approach.
Conduct prospective clinical studies to assess the impact of AI algorithms in practice.
Clinically validate each automatically learned link in a Bayesian network to ensure it reflects a plausible causal mechanism rather than a spurious correlation.
Prefer inherently interpretable models with stable, global explanations that quantify uncertainty over post-hoc explanation methods for clinical decision support.
Determine actionable thresholds for probabilistic AI outputs through dedicated studies and consensus within each ICU.

screen.reason: This is a clinical perspective article discussing the advantages, explainability, and deployment considerations of Bayesian Networks for sepsis prediction in the ICU.
